text:
A: Alright, mate! How you doing?
B: Hi. Erm, good, thanks. I'm Bethany.
A: Darren. You look about as done with this as I am.
B: Sorry. No, it's been nice, mostly. I'm just a bit tired.
A: Don't apologise, love. Where you calling from?
B: Bridgwater.
A: Get away! Me too! Whereabouts?
B: Near the town centre. Above a takeaway, sort of off the main road.
A: Not the chippy? With the blue sign?
B: Yeah, that one.
A: I've had more cod out of there than I've had hot dinners. Well, they were hot dinners. You know what I mean. Small world, innit. What are the chances, eh?
B: I know. I thought you looked a bit familiar in your photo, actually. Not like I know you. Just... like someone from here.
A: It's the face. Everyone in Bridgwater's got the face. You working?
B: Not at the minute. I volunteer at the hospice shop, Tuesdays and Thursdays. I had a packing job but it ended.
A: Same boat, me. Back went. Was on the forklifts off the M5 for years.
B: Oh, that's where Kieran works. My boyfriend. He drives forklift there.
A: Kieran? Tall lad? Bit quiet?
B: Erm, yeah, quite tall. Quite quiet. Kieran Hollis.
A: Might've seen him about. Can't put a face to it, my memory's shot. You tell him Darren says the canteen pasties are a crime.
B: I will. He says that as well.
A: Good lad. So what are you after, job-wise?
B: I'm not sure really. Something steady. I sort of thought maybe a garden centre, or the library. But I get really nervous about interviews. I cancelled one once. I just couldn't make myself go.
A: Oh, mate, I've done worse. I walked out of one halfway through 'cause the bloke was talking to me like I was thick. Wasn't proud of it. Jobcentre weren't proud of it either.
B: Did you get in trouble?
A: Bit of a telling off. Water off a duck's back. Well, sort of. Honestly, though, a library, you'd be brilliant. You've got the library look.
B: That's what someone else said. The Craig one.
A: The grumpy one? Don't listen to him. Here, you going carnival this year?
B: Yeah, I go every year. I watch from near the Cornhill, 'cause the crowds are a bit much further down.
A: Never missed one. Not once. Last year's winner, though, I'm still not having it. That cart from the year before was miles better, the lights on it—
B: The one with the owls? I drew that one.
A: You drew it? Get away. You want to show the club that, they'd—
